verses.text: After these things Yahweh’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”
Abram said, “Lord  Yahweh, what will you give me, since I go childless, and he who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?”
Abram said, “Behold, to me you have given no children : and, behold, one born in my house is my heir.”
Behold, Yahweh’s word came to him, saying, “This man will not be your heir, but he who will come out of your own body will be your heir.”
Yahweh brought him outside, and said, “Look now toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” He said to Abram, “So will your offspring  be.”
He believed in Yahweh, who credited it to him for righteousness.
He said to Abram, “I am Yahweh who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you this land to inherit it.”
He said, “Lord Yahweh, how will I know that I will inherit it?”
He said to him, “Bring me a heifer three years old, a female goat three years old, a ram three years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”
He brought him all these, and divided them in the middle, and laid each half opposite the other; but he didn’t divide the birds.
The birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
When the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram. Now terror and great darkness fell on him.
He said to Abram, “Know for sure that your offspring  will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them. They will afflict them four hundred years.
I will also judge that nation, whom they will serve. Afterward they will come out with great wealth,
but you will go to your fathers in peace. You will be buried at a good old age.
In the fourth generation they will come here again, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full.”
It came to pass that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold, a smoking furnace, and a flaming torch passed between these pieces.
In that day Yahweh made a covenant with Abram, saying, “I have given this land to your offspring,  from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,
the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”

footnotes.content: After so much leaving and wandering, Abram hears the word of Yahweh again. I find it tender that the Lord begins not with rebuke, but with 'Do not be afraid' - He knows the weight that settles on a heart waiting on His promise. What peace to know that the God who calls us is also our shield and our exceedingly great reward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram speaks honestly to the Lord, calling Him 'Lord Yahweh' as he brings his grief before Him. I have learned it is no lack of faith to say what aches in us - childlessness loomed large for him, and Eliezer of Damascus stood as the one who would inherit by default. Our Lord is never put off by honest prayer from a burdened heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram lays out the hard fact plainly: the Lord has given him no child, so a servant born in his house must be heir. I know the temptation to count only what we see, but the God who promised is not bound by what we see. Even in honest disappointment, His word is not finished speaking.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word of Yahweh comes directly to Abram: the heir will not be Eliezer, but one who comes from his own body. I take comfort that the Lord does not dismiss Abram's question - He answers it with precision. When God gives a promise, He is faithful to specify it, and He is faithful to keep it in His own way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh brings Abram outside under the open sky and bids him look up to count the stars. For a man with no child, the heavens are about to preach the faithfulness of God. I have found that sometimes the Lord must draw us away from our small room of worry to show us the magnitude of what He has said He will do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This is one of those precious anchors: Abram believed in Yahweh, and He credited it to him for righteousness. It is not the strength of Abram's grasp, but the faithfulness of the One he trusted that is counted as righteousness - a truth that points us to our greater Abram, Jesus Christ, who is our righteousness before God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh reminds Abram who He is: the same One who brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees to give him this land. I take heart that the God who began to lead us is the God who binds Himself to complete what He has spoken. His faithfulness to past acts gives us courage to trust His future promises.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again Abram asks, 'Lord Yahweh, how will I know that I will inherit it?' I am grateful the Lord does not chide him for wanting assurance. Faith clings to the promise, and the God of faithfulness condescends to give a way for that faith to rest more firmly on Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh tells Abram to bring specific animals - a heifer, a female goat, a ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon, all three years old. To us it seems strange, but Abram would have known this was the language of a solemn covenant. The Lord is not stingy with making His word sure; He stoops to speak in a way His servant can understand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram obeys exactly as commanded, cutting the larger animals in two and laying the halves opposite each other, but leaving the birds whole. In ancient covenant making, passing between the pieces meant taking the oath upon oneself. It is a sobering picture of the cost of keeping covenant - and one that makes us all the more grateful that Jesus has passed through for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Birds of prey swoop down on the carcasses, and Abram drives them away. I see a small but faithful act: he guards the place of the covenant until the Lord moves. How often our part is simply to watch and ward off what would tear at the things God has promised, trusting Him to do the greater work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As the sun goes down, deep sleep falls on Abram, and terror with great darkness comes over him. The one whom God has called 'fear not' now trembles in the presence of the Holy One. I find it both humbling and merciful - to draw near to God is awe-full, and He kindly prepares Abram for the revelation to come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh speaks of sure things to come: Abram's offspring will be foreigners in a land not theirs, will serve them, and be afflicted four hundred years. The God who gives the promise also tells Abram of the long road before it. I take comfort that our Father does not hide the cost, but He never hides Himself from those He loves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord Himself will judge the nation that enslaves Abram's offspring, and they will come out with great wealth. I love that the promise-keeper is also the just judge. He sees the oppression of His people, and in due time He acts for them - a glimpse of the greater redemption He has planned for all who belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abram himself will go to his fathers in peace and be buried at a good old age. The Lord tenderly gives him rest before the affliction comes upon his descendants. There is grace in that - not all of the hard things fall on one generation, and the faithful servant is gathered to his fathers in the peace of the God who keeps His word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the fourth generation they will return, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full. I am struck that the Lord is patient - He delays judgment until the measure is complete, and He times deliverance according to His faithful purposes. His timing is never hasty, and never late.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When the sun went down and it was dark, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces. Abram is asleep, but the Lord Himself walks the path of the covenant alone. What mercy - if the oath depended on Abram keeping it, we would be undone. But the faithful God passes between the pieces for His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: On that day Yahweh made a covenant with Abram, giving the land from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates. The covenant is made by the One who cannot lie. I rest in this: the ultimate inheritance for all who believe is not merely land, but a new creation, secured for us by Jesus who is the true Seed of Abraham.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Kenites are named among those whose land is promised. They were a small, nomadic people, yet the Lord does not overlook any group in His purposes. It reminds me that the God who makes great promises also takes notice of the least, and His covenant reaches farther than we can see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Hittites, Perizzites, and Rephaim are listed - peoples who occupied that land in Abram's day. The promise was sure, though possession lay far off. I take courage: God often gives promises that will only be fully known by future generations, but He is already faithful to bring every word to pass.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites complete the list - the very peoples Israel would later encounter. The Lord names them all, knowing each by name. What a comfort that our God is not vague in His promises: He sees every person and every place, and He will accomplish all He has purposed for the glory of His name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
